model-knowledge.note: Seed pending harvest; Wikipedia and vendor spec sources egress-blocked in this environment.

gaps: Dual-GPU flagships (GTX 590, GTX 690, GTX Titan Z) deliberately omitted: one board carries two GPUs, so shaders/memBusBits/vramGB cannot be expressed in this schema without either doubling the shader count (which would make the fitted perf model wildly overestimate them, since AFR scaling is 0-70% and modern titles do not support SLI at all) or halving the marketed VRAM. Better absent than silently wrong.

OEM-only SKUs omitted for lack of confident specs: GTX 555, GTX 545, GT 545, GT 530, GT 420, GT 405, GTX 460 v2, GTX 645, GTX 660 OEM (1152-core), GTX 760 Ti (OEM), GTX 745, GT 605, GT 635, GT 705, GT 1010.

Ultra-low-end parts whose marketing name covers multiple different GPUs omitted: GT 630 (GF108 / GK107 / GK208 revisions), GT 620, GT 640 GDDR5 and GK208 revisions, GT 730 GF108 128-bit DDR3 revision. Splitting them correctly needs the PCI-ID tables that are egress-blocked here.
Regional/market variants omitted: GTX 1060 5GB (China), RTX 4090 D, RTX 5090 D, RTX 4070 GDDR6 (2024 respin), RTX 3050 8GB GA107 115W respin.

No RTX 50 "Super" refresh parts are included. As of this seed I have no reliable shader/clock/VRAM figures for any 2026 Blackwell refresh, and the brief forbids guessing. If such parts shipped, they are missing.
pciIds is absent on every record - PCI device IDs come from driver INF tables (pci-ids / TechPowerUp), both egress-blocked. The alias resolver gets nothing from this seed.
lengthMm is null on ~80% of records. Only Founders Edition / reference lengths I am confident of are populated; AIB board length variance is 40-80mm and guessing it would be worse than a null.
driverEolDate is populated only for Fermi and Kepler. Maxwell/Pascal/Volta moved to legacy after the seed cutoff and I am not confident of the exact branch end date.
fp32TFLOPS is null on all 17 Fermi records - see uncertainties, the shader hot clock is not representable in this schema.

AIB-only double-VRAM variants below Kepler are not split out (GTX 460 2GB, GTX 560 Ti 2GB, GTX 650 Ti 2GB, GTX 750 Ti 1GB). Kepler-era splits that Nvidia listed itself (680/670/660 Ti/660/770/780) are included.
Mobile parts, Quadro/Tesla/workstation parts and all pre-Fermi GeForce (GT200 and older) are out of remit and absent by design.
uncertainties: FERMI CLOCK DOMAIN: Fermi runs its shader array at 2x the core clock (GTX 580: 772 MHz core / 1544 MHz shader). GpuRecord has no shader-clock field, and the validator computes fp32 from shaders*boostClockMHz*2, which would give exactly half the true figure. I therefore set baseClockMHz = boostClockMHz = core clock (Fermi has no boost algorithm) and left fp32TFLOPS null. True FP32 for reference: GTX 480 1.345, GTX 580 1.581, GTX 570 1.405, GTX 560 Ti 1.263, GTX 460 1GB 0.907 TFLOPS.

GTX 16 SERIES FEATURE LEVEL: set to dxFeatureLevel 12_2 / shaderModel 6_7 per the brief. Nvidia does not market TU116/TU117 as DirectX 12 Ultimate because they have no RT cores, and the driver reports feature level 12_1. The load-bearing fact is unchanged and correct either way: meshShaders true, rayTracing false - a GTX 1660 does run Alan Wake 2 and does not run an RT-required title.

GTX 970 vramGB is 4, which is the marketed and physically-present configuration, but the last 512MB runs on a crippled partition at ~28GB/s. Any VRAM-ceiling gate treating it as a flat 4GB will be optimistic by roughly 0.5GB.

Asymmetric memory configurations reported at peak: GTX 660, GTX 660 Ti, GTX 550 Ti and GTX 1050 3GB do not have uniform bandwidth across the whole framebuffer. memBandwidthGBs is the headline peak figure.

RTX 5050: boost clock 2572 MHz is moderate confidence and the base clock is null. Shaders (2560), 8GB GDDR6 128-bit, 130W are higher confidence. Of all RTX 50 records this is the one most likely to need correction.

GT 730 (both variants), GT 720, GT 740 and GT 640: TDP and the base=boost assumption are moderate confidence. These GK107/GK208 parts have no published boost clock, so boostClockMHz repeats the core clock, which makes fp32TFLOPS a ceiling rather than a sustained figure.

recommendedPsuW is Nvidia's published minimum system power, not a measured transient figure. RTX 30/40/50 parts with large power spikes (3080 Ti, 3090 Ti, 4090) can trip protection on nominally-compliant units.
powerConnectors describes the Founders Edition / reference design. AIB variants routinely differ (e.g. RTX 3090 FE is 12-pin, AIB cards are 3x8-pin; RTX 5070 AIB cards ship with 1x8-pin).
caps.vulkanVersion is driver-branch dependent rather than a hardware property. Fermi is null (no confident answer), Kepler is pinned at 1.2 because its driver branch froze before Vulkan 1.3 shipped.

shaderModel for Kepler and Maxwell 1 is bucketed at 6_0 and for Maxwell 2/Pascal/Volta at 6_5. This follows the brief's coarse mapping; in practice Nvidia's modern driver reports a higher SM level on these parts than their feature support justifies.
processNm for Ada Lovelace and Blackwell is given as 5 (TSMC 4N and 4NP are 5nm-class nodes, not a distinct 4nm node). Pascal GP107/GP108 are 14 (Samsung) while the rest of Pascal is 16 (TSMC).

Launch dates for AIB double-VRAM variants (GTX 680 4GB, 670 4GB, 660 3GB, 660 Ti 3GB, 770 4GB, 780 6GB, GTX 960 4GB) are month-granularity approximations of when those configurations reached retail, not Nvidia launch announcements.
driverEolDate 2019-04 (Fermi) and 2024-09 (Kepler) are the end of extended security-update support at month granularity, not the last Game Ready driver date.

Titan parts are included although the remit made them optional. The four NVIDIA-branded ones (Titan X Pascal, Titan Xp, Titan V, Titan RTX) use nvidia-titan-* ids since they are not GeForce-branded; GTX Titan / Titan Black / Titan X (Maxwell) use nvidia-geforce-* ids.
